name: The Three-Action Economy
subtitle: The heart of a turn in Pathfinder

blocks.t: On your turn, you get **three actions** and **one reaction**. Actions are spent to do things like Stride, Strike, Raise a Shield, or Cast a Spell. You can spend them in any order, and you may spend fewer than three if you wish.

Some activities cost **two or three actions** and must be spent all at once — you can't split them across other actions. You can use a reaction only when its trigger occurs, and only once per turn unless an ability says otherwise.

items: **Stride** (1 action) — move up to your Speed.
**Strike** (1 action) — make a melee or ranged attack against a creature in range.
**Raise a Shield** (1 action) — gain your shield's bonus to AC until the start of your next turn.
**Step** (1 action) — move 5 feet without provoking reactions.

name: Degrees of Success
subtitle: Critical Success, Success, Failure, Critical Failure

blocks.t: Every check has **four possible results**. Roll a d20, add modifiers, and compare to a DC. If you beat the DC by 10 or more it's a **critical success**; if you fail by 10 or more it's a **critical failure**. Otherwise it's a plain success or failure.

A **natural 20** on the die improves the result by one step (success → critical success), and a **natural 1** worsens it by one step. Effects with a saving throw use the same degrees: a target that succeeds takes no effect, and one that critically succeeds might suffer no effect at all.

name: Hero Points
subtitle: Rerolls, stability, and recovery

blocks.t: You gain **1 Hero Point** at the start of each session, and the GM awards more for heroic moments. You can have at most 3.

items: **Reroll** — spend 1 point to reroll a d20 you just rolled, taking the better result.
**Recovery** — if a condition would reduce you to 0 HP, spend 1 point to instead stay at 1 HP and become stable.

name: Saving Throws
subtitle: Fortitude, Reflex, and Will

blocks.t: When a hazard, spell, or foe's ability threatens you, you attempt a saving throw: a d20 roll against the effect's DC. The three saves cover different dangers.

rows: Poison, disease, being disarmed, body-weakening effects
Falling, area effects like fireballs, being grabbed or knocked prone

name: Critical Hits
subtitle: Double damage, deadlier effects

blocks.t: When you roll a **critical hit** on an attack (natural 20, or beating the target's AC by 10), **double the damage** you roll — including bonus dice and bonus damage, but not extra damage from sources like persistent damage.
For a critical **failure** on an attack roll, you simply miss — but if you critically fail a saving throw, you suffer the effect's worst degree, which is often **double damage** as well.

name: Death and Dying
subtitle: What happens at 0 HP

blocks.t: When you're reduced to **0 Hit Points**, you gain the **dying** condition. You're knocked out and can't act, and on each of your turns you attempt a **recovery check** (flat DC 10): success stabilizes you at 1 HP, critical success wakes you up, failure increases your dying value, and critical failure increases it by 2.

If your dying value ever reaches your **dying max** (usually 4, more if you have feats like Toughness), you die. Taking damage while dying increases the value too. A hero can instead spend a Hero Point to stabilize at 1 HP.
